headline: High: shared filesystem, MCP, and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can use MCP and read/write filesystems, and Windsurf exposes clipboard plus workspace files while nullclaw can ingest web content and files. That creates a plausible instruction-bridging path through shared files or MCP content, even though no direct shared channel is explicitly documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace directory or MCP server, attacker-controlled content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF either agent parses file or clipboard content as trusted prompts, injection becomes viable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and MCP servers per agent.
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent files.
Require explicit human approval before executing instructions sourced from files.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and prompt-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files; Windsurf touches source code and open files, with shared state via local filesystem and clipboard. A shared workspace or filesystem would let sensitive data flow between them, and both have broad network egress. This is a default-risk pathway, not just an unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace, files can cross from nullclaw to Windsurf.
IF either agent uploads file contents to its backend, secrets in shared files may leave the host.
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers.
Keep secrets out of shared workspaces.
Mount sensitive directories read-only or not at all.
Turn off automatic file upload where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell, modify git state, write files, and use MCP. Windsurf shares state via local filesystem, while nullclaw has durable shared memory and broad session scope. Concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can corrupt git state or overwrite each other without locking, which matches the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, concurrent commits or rebases can conflict.
IF both agents write to the same directory without locks, file corruption or lost updates can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone.
Serialize git operations with a lock file.
Disable auto-commit or auto-merge flows.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can ingest web content, files, and webhooks, and Windsurf can act on workspace files and MCP outputs. If Windsurf treats nullclaw-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or terminal actions. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Windsurf consumes nullclaw output as a task spec without verification, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF nullclaw writes webhook or workspace artifacts that Windsurf later executes, errors can cascade into downstream changes.
mitigations: Require human review before execution of cross-agent outputs.
Add schema validation for handoff files.
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted by default.
Use read-only handoff directories.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, conversation history, and audit logs, while Windsurf handles source code and open files with local filesystem sharing. If regulated or secret-bearing data is placed into Windsurf's workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge from nullclaw's handling. The profiles do not prove a specific legal breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or personal data are stored in a shared workspace, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the deployment requires a specific residency or retention policy, the pair may violate it unless aligned.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Restrict each agent to the minimum necessary data class.
Review vendor terms before enabling shared storage.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows.
